Title: Battery bank and Charger Maintenance

Document No.:[SMP/E&I/005]

Issue Date: 15-09-2025

Page 2 of 5

### 1.0 Purpose:

To establish a standardized and safe maintenance procedure for battery banks and chargers, ensuring personnel safety, equipment reliability, and compliance with applicable electrical and environmental standards.

### 2.0 Scope:

This procedure applies to all maintenance activities involving battery banks (VRLA, Ni-Cd, Lead-Acid) and associated battery chargers, including inspection, testing, servicing, and replacement. It is intended for use by authorized electrical maintenance personnel across all operational areas.

### 2.1 Definitions and Abbreviations

- SMP: Safe Maintenance Procedure
- VRLA: Valve Regulated Lead Acid
- PTW: Permit to Work
- LOTOTO: Lock Out Tag Out Try Out
- CCR: Central Control Room
- IR: Insulation Resistance
- SOC: State of Charge
- SOH: State of Health

### 3.0 Safety, Health & Environment Consideration

### 3.1 General Safety Rules:

- Only authorized and trained personnel shall perform maintenance.
- Obtain a valid PTW and follow LOTOTO procedures.
- Disconnect power supply before starting any maintenance.
- No smoking or open flames near battery bank.
- Use insulated tools and follow lockout/tagout procedures.
- Only trained and authorized personnel should perform maintenance.
- Ensure the presence of a standby person during the activity.
- Verify absence of voltage before starting work.
- Avoid short circuits across battery terminals.
- Use insulated tools and wear PPE as per the matrix.

### 3.2 Health Considerations:

- Avoid contact with battery electrolyte.
- Wash exposed skin immediately with clean water.
- Use proper lifting techniques to prevent injury when handling batteries.
- Ensure the technician is physically fit and not fatigued.
- Avoid direct contact with battery electrolyte.
- Use eye wash stations in case of acid contact.

### 3.3 Environment Considerations:

- Ensure proper ventilation in the battery room.
- Neutralize and clean up any acid spills immediately.
- Dispose of used batteries and electrolyte per environmental regulations.

### 3.4 Specific Safety Standard requirement:

- Refer to IEC 60896, IEEE Std 1188 for stationary batteries.
- Follow NFPA 70E for electrical safety practices.
- Electrical Safety Standards (IS/IEC)

### 3.5 Hazards:

- Electrical shock
- Acid burns
- Hydrogen gas accumulation (explosion risk)
- Fire hazard
- Slips due to electrolyte spillage
- Short circuits

### 3.6 PPE-Matrix:

|  Activity / PPE | Helmet | Safety Shoes | Goggles | Electrical hand gloves | Arc Flash suit | Face shield | Reflecting Jacket | Dust Mask  |

|  Voltage checking by using Multi meter | √ | √ | √ | √ | √ | √ | √ |   |

### 3.7 Environment Control:

- Exhaust fans must be operational.
- Use acid-proof trays/floor under batteries.
- Dispose of used electrolyte, cleaning cloths, and containers as per hazardous waste guidelines.

### 3.8 Environmental Requirements:

- Ensure safe handling and disposal of acid and lead materials.
- Maintain spill containment kits in vicinity.
- Ambient temperature: 20–30°C
- Humidity: < 85% RH (non-condensing)
- Dust-free and well-ventilated area

### 4.0 Quality consideration:

- Ensure all batteries are maintained as per OEM specs
- Charger parameters are logged post-maintenance.
- Use OEM approved spares
- Use tested tools and equipment

### 5.0 Maintenance Control and Considerations:

- Use checklist and logbook for routine and preventive maintenance.
- All maintenance data shall be recorded and verified.
- Follow OEM-recommended maintenance schedules.
- Maintain a log of all maintenance activities.

### 6.0 Maintenance Procedure

#### 6.1 Routine maintenance Procedure-Activities

|  SL.NO | ACTIVITIES | Safety Precautions | Responsibility  |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
|  1 | Obtain PTW and isolate power supply | Follow LOTOTO procedure | Authorized Technician  |
|  2 | Visual inspection of battery bank and charger | Use insulated tools, gloves  |   |
|  3 | Check electrolyte level (for flooded batteries) | Wear acid-resistant PPE  |   |
|  4 | Measure battery voltage, specific gravity (if applicable), and temperature | Use calibrated instruments  |   |
|  5 | Check charger output voltage and current | Ensure charger is in float mode  |   |
|  6 | Inspect and tighten all electrical connections | Use insulated tools  |   |
|  7 | Check for corrosion, cracks, or leakage in battery casing | Replace damaged units  |   |
|  8 | Perform IR test (if applicable) | Discharge before and after test  |   |
|  9 | Verify charger alarms, indicators, and control settings | Refer to OEM manual  |   |
|  10 | Record all readings and observations in the logbook |   |   |
|  11 | Restore power and close PTW after completion | Follow LT isolation SOP  |   |

#### 6.2 Pre maintenance Checks

- Inform concerned departments of any potential power interruptions.
- Arrange standby power if required.
- Ensure availability of tools, PPE, and spares.
- Confirm battery system is isolated.
- Check for acid leaks.
- Verify PPE availability.

#### 6.3 Shutdown Procedure (If applicable) :

- Notify relevant departments.
- Follow LT isolation SOP and Isolate power using lockout/tagout
- Ensure charger and battery bank are safely isolated.
- Power down charger using standard shutdown procedure.

#### 6.4 Abnormal condition handling:

- In case of bulging batteries, isolate immediately.
- For overheating or smoke, activate emergency stop and ventilate area.
- If battery temperature is high, stop charging and allow cooling.
- If charger trips or shows fault, isolate and inspect as per charger troubleshooting SOP.
- If battery voltage is abnormally low, check for deep discharge and consult OEM if needed

### 6.5 Emergency maintenance procedure:

- Use emergency PPE and isolate faulty component.
- Contact electrical and safety team immediately.
- Follow emergency response plan for acid spills or gas leaks.

### 6.6 Special maintenance instructions

- Perform equalization charge as per OEM recommendation.
- Replace batteries older than recommended life span or showing failure signs.
- Consult OEM for any major repair or replacement.
- Avoid simultaneous maintenance on both charger and battery bank unless necessary

### 7.0 Troubleshooting:

|  Issue | Possible Cause | Action  |
| --- | --- | --- |
|  Charger not working | Blown fuse, power failure | Check input supply, replace fuse  |
|  Battery not charging | Loose connection, faulty cell | Inspect terminals, replace cell  |
|  High battery temperature | Overcharging | Switch to float mode, allow cooling  |
|  Low voltage alarm | Deep discharge | Perform boost charge  |
|  Acid leakage | Damaged casing | Replace battery, clean area  |

### 8.0 Cross-references:

- Battery & Charger OEM Manuals
- Preventive Maintenance Schedule
- Electrical Safety Guidelines
- LT Isolation SOP
- HIRO document
- Emergency Response Plan
